analysis.title: Fast Take: Take-Two Interactive Software Inc
key_insights: GTA VI received a 99 Metacritic rating, matching the highest in video game history but with more reviews.
Sensor Tower estimates 17M+ units and $1.65B revenue to date, versus UBS estimates of 37M units and $3.3B gross sales in the December quarter.

UBS estimates GTA V sold 16M units in 3 days and 29M sell-in over 6 weeks. Using that curve, which UBS calls imperfect, about 20M units and $1.8B of sales in 3 days would be needed to hit the UBS December quarter estimate.
UBS keeps a Buy rating and a $295 price target on Take-Two, 44.7% above the $203.93 close on 17 Nov 2026. The stock's 52-week range is $189.69 to $258.41.
UBS FY03/27E EPS is $7.21 against consensus of $7.00. FY03/28E EPS is $10.86 against consensus of $9.97.
UBS fiscal Q3 (December quarter) EPS estimate is $4.63 against consensus of $4.24.

market_movers.rationale: The GTA VI review score of 99 supports the launch, and the December quarter estimate of 37M units and $3.3B gross sales is above early Sensor Tower tracking of 17M+ units and $1.65B revenue to date.

earnings_insights: UBS December quarter (fiscal Q3 FY03/27E) EPS estimate $4.63 vs consensus $4.24. Both are estimates, not reported figures.
UBS FY03/27E EPS $7.21 (UBS diluted, estimate) vs consensus $7.00. FY03/28E EPS $10.86 (estimate) vs consensus $9.97.
UBS fiscal Q4 FY03/27E EPS estimate $1.23 vs consensus $1.30.
UBS December quarter estimate: 37M units and $3.3B gross sales for GTA VI. Sensor Tower estimate to date: 17M+ units and $1.65B revenue.
UBS FY03/27E revenue estimate $8,694M, up from $6,656M in FY03/26. FY03/28E revenue estimate $9,092M.
risk_factors: Macroeconomic headwinds and lower discretionary spending by consumers.
Dependence on launching new hit games. Weak launches would put financial results at risk.
Negative consumer sentiment or public scrutiny, IT or communications outages, and failure to obtain licenses at reasonable cost.
IP and copyright claims, and shifts in user preferences.
